ARTICLE GAP: the Order of Owens has its own wiki article built from an operator-supplied roster; the Knights of Kanawana is the same kind of institution -- a named honour with a citation, a crest, the camp motto, and a 29-year roll -- and appears nowhere except passing mentions in traditions-and-culture.md and order-of-owens.md. note: A COHORT TRACKED TWO YEARS ON. Christina Kaminski, Manon Griffin, Lily Foris, Emma Copeman and Tessa Dixon are ALL on the Adventurer Girls 2008 board -- five of the eight campers here were together in 2008 and are together again in 2010. Every camper carries a nickname. Evan Frenkel as LIT here agrees with the KB's existing note (f_1764) that the 2008 Rounds winner was a 2010 LIT; the surname is spelled FRENKEL on this board and FRANKEL on the 2008 paddle, both recorded as found.

COMPLETE. Worth noting the CRAFT, which separates this board from every camper plaque in the album: the lettering is routed and the central tree is relief-carved, made with woodworking tools by people who had them. All four names are francophone, and Claude Beaulieu reappears on the Staff 02 plaque -- a five-year span for the maintenance crew, the only non-programme staff commemorated anywhere in the collection.

COMPLETE, and IT SETTLES A FLAG RAISED EARLIER IN THIS AUDIT. At rangers-1964.jpg I noted that f_1676 describes a nearby carving as reading 'Kamp Kanawana 1994', that its final digits were illegible in that frame, and that its style looked mid-century -- possibly 1944. This tray is that style exactly: a bordered relief-carved panel with a tent, a canoe and crossed implements, reading KAMP - KANAWANA 1999. The object beside the Rangers paddle is this piece or its twin, and the year is 1999. My own 'possibly 1944' speculation was wrong, and I am glad I flagged it rather than acting on it -- a stylistic impression pointed the wrong way by half a century.

low_conf: nearly every name here -- the fact's warning about physical obstruction is correct and understated: armoured electrical conduit and a bundle of red and white cabling run directly across the board's right-hand list, and the lettering is small and dark on dark red
note: Cut as a red canoe with two carved paddler figures standing proud of it, KK monogram amidships -- the most sculptural object in the album. The roster is the least readable part and my transcription should be treated as provisional throughout. RE-PHOTOGRAPHY WOULD FIX THIS ONE EASILY: the problem is the wiring in front of the board, not the paint on it.

COMPLETE. Painted with a bear paw and a palm tree, the aside 'Maybe it's a Beaver?' answering the paw. JESS DOBRINSKI IS ALSO ON THE MALIBU 2001 BOARD as Jessica Dobrinski, five years earlier and on the same section's trip -- camper to leader, most likely. Sybil G-Stock is an LIT in 2008.

low_conf: Gillian [?] -- surname lost in the mottled paint
note: COMPLICATES A LEAD I OFFERED EARLIER, AND SHOULD. At rangers-2003.jpg I noted that f_1678 records the second Rangers co-ordinator only as '[-] Tanguy' and suggested AURELIE TANGUY of the Staff 02 plaque as a candidate for the missing first name. THIS BOARD NAMES A CHARLES-ERIC TANGUAY, IN 2003 ITSELF -- the same season as the Rangers board, against Aurelie's adjacent one. There are now two candidates, the newer one better placed by year, and the surname is spelled TANGUAY here against TANGUY on the Rangers board. My earlier suggestion should not be allowed to stand as the leading one; both are candidates and neither is an identification. Cut in the shape of a tree with three hanging tags naming the trip's lakes.
